$comment: Provisional manifest written with story B2 so the MCP server can be built and tested. Story F1 takes it over: it must match the real components in src/components/ui. Format: docs/API.md#manifest.

components.name: Alert
components.summary: A message in the flow of the page that explains a state: info, success, warning or error.

props.name: variant
props.description: destructive says what failed and what to do next; success, warning and info are Atlas additions. Pair each with its icon.

props.name: role
props.description: Defaults to "alert" for destructive and "status" for the other tones.

examples.title: Warning with icon and title
examples.code:
<Alert variant="warning">
  <TriangleAlert />
  <AlertTitle>Stock is low</AlertTitle>
  <AlertDescription>3 items left. Reorder before Friday.</AlertDescription>
</Alert>

do: Start with the status icon, then a title that says what happened, then the next step.
Put a dismiss Button (ghost, size icon, aria-label "Dismiss") in AlertAction.
dont: Don't use an Alert to confirm a finished action; use a toast.
Don't rely on the color alone: keep the icon and the words.

components.name: Badge
components.summary: A short label for a status or a category, next to the thing it describes.

props.name: variant
props.description: Status variants (success, warning, info, destructive) always carry a text label.

props.name: asChild
props.description: Render the child element (for example a link) with the badge styles.

examples.title: Order status
examples.code: <Badge variant="success">Paid</Badge>

do: Pair a status variant with its icon and a word: <CircleCheck /> Paid.
dont: Don't use a colored dot or a badge with no text for a status.
Don't round badges into pills.

components.name: Breadcrumb
components.summary: The path from a section to the current page, with a link for each level above it.

props.name: aria-label
props.description: Name of the navigation landmark.

props.name: asChild
props.description: Render the router's own link (e.g. <Link>) with the breadcrumb styles.

props.name: children
props.description: What goes between two levels; a slash unless you pass something else.

examples.title: Note path
examples.code:
<Breadcrumb>
  <BreadcrumbList>
    <BreadcrumbItem>
      <BreadcrumbLink href="/explore">Explore</BreadcrumbLink>
    </BreadcrumbItem>
    <BreadcrumbSeparator />
    <BreadcrumbItem>
      <BreadcrumbLink href="/explore?type=decision">Decisions</BreadcrumbLink>
    </BreadcrumbItem>
    <BreadcrumbSeparator />
    <BreadcrumbItem>
      <BreadcrumbPage className="font-mono">frame-supplier.md</BreadcrumbPage>
    </BreadcrumbItem>
  </BreadcrumbList>
</Breadcrumb>

do: Link every level above the page; the last item is a BreadcrumbPage, which carries aria-current="page".
Put a BreadcrumbSeparator between items, never inside a BreadcrumbItem.
dont: Don't use a breadcrumb as the main navigation or for steps of a flow.

components.name: Button
components.summary: Starts an action. One primary button per view.

props.name: variant
props.description: default is the one primary action; destructive deletes or cancels something for good, after a Dialog; link sits inside a sentence.

props.name: size
props.description: default and icon are 40 px (44 px on touch); lg is 48 px. Icon buttons need an aria-label.

props.name: asChild
props.description: Render the child element (for example a link) with the button styles.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Prefer explaining why an action is unavailable over disabling it silently.

examples.title: Primary action
examples.code: <Button>Save order</Button>

examples.title: Icon button
examples.code:
<Button variant="ghost" size="icon" aria-label="Copy command">
  <Copy />
</Button>

do: Label with a verb and an object: "Save order", "Copy command".
Make one default (primary) button per view; the rest outline, secondary or ghost.
dont: Don't put two default (primary) buttons in the same view.
Don't label a button OK or Submit.

components.name: Card
components.summary: A bordered surface that groups content about one thing.

examples.title: Card with header and content
examples.code:
<Card>
  <CardHeader>
    <CardTitle>Orders</CardTitle>
    <CardDescription>Last 30 days</CardDescription>
  </CardHeader>
  <CardContent>…</CardContent>
</Card>

do: Use a Card to frame a table, a form or a summary.
dont: Don't build a grid of identical cards with an icon in a rounded square.

components.name: Checkbox
components.summary: An on or off choice, alone or in a list of filters; a dash for a group that is partly on.

props.name: checked
props.description: Controlled state; indeterminate shows a dash for a group that is partly checked.

props.name: defaultChecked
props.description: Starting state when uncontrolled.

props.name: onCheckedChange
props.description: Called with the new state: true or false.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Shown at half opacity and cannot be changed.

examples.title: Filter list
examples.code: Note types

do: Wrap the checkbox and its text in one <label>, so the text names it and clicking the text toggles it.
Leave at least 12 px (gap-3) next to it: its 40 px hit area reaches past the 16 px box.
dont: Don't use a checkbox for an action that runs at once; use a Button.

components.name: Collapsible
components.summary: A section that opens and closes from a button, such as a table of properties.

props.name: defaultOpen
props.description: Starts open when uncontrolled.

props.name: open
props.description: Controlled state, with onOpenChange.

props.name: asChild
props.description: Use your own Button as the trigger; it gets aria-expanded and data-state.

examples.title: Properties
examples.code:
<Collapsible defaultOpen>
  <CollapsibleTrigger asChild>
    <Button variant="ghost" className="-ml-3 [&[data-state=open]>svg]:rotate-180">
      Properties
      <ChevronDown />
    </Button>
  </CollapsibleTrigger>
  <CollapsibleContent>
    <dl className="grid grid-cols-[auto_1fr] gap-x-3 gap-y-1.5 font-mono text-[13px]">
      <dt className="text-muted-foreground">type</dt>
      <dd className="m-0">decision</dd>
      <dt className="text-muted-foreground">updated</dt>
      <dd className="m-0">2026-03-14</dd>
    </dl>
  </CollapsibleContent>
</Collapsible>

do: Make the trigger a Button (asChild) whose text names the section, with a chevron that turns when it opens.
dont: Don't hide the only copy of something people need to finish a task inside a closed section.

components.name: Command
components.summary: A searchable list of actions or items, opened with ⌘K or inline.

props.name: title
props.description: Hidden title read by screen readers.

props.name: showCloseButton
props.description: Shows the close button in the corner.

examples.title: Command palette
examples.code:
<CommandDialog open={open} onOpenChange={setOpen}>
  <CommandInput placeholder="Search orders…" />
  <CommandList>
    <CommandEmpty>No orders found.</CommandEmpty>
    <CommandGroup heading="Orders">
      <CommandItem>#1042 · Ana Ruiz</CommandItem>
    </CommandGroup>
  </CommandList>
</CommandDialog>

do: Always include CommandEmpty with what to try next.
dont: Don't use Command for a short fixed list; use Select.

components.name: Dialog
components.summary: A modal window for a short task or a confirmation. Focus stays inside until it closes.

props.name: showCloseButton
props.description: Shows the × button in the corner.

props.name: showCloseButton
props.description: Adds an outline "Close" button to the footer.

examples.title: Confirm a refund
examples.code:
<Dialog>
  <DialogTrigger asChild>
    <Button variant="destructive">Refund order</Button>
  </DialogTrigger>
  <DialogContent>
    <DialogHeader>
      <DialogTitle>Refund order #1042?</DialogTitle>
      <DialogDescription>The customer gets $84.00 back. This can't be undone.</DialogDescription>
    </DialogHeader>
    <DialogFooter>
      <DialogClose asChild>
        <Button variant="outline">Keep order</Button>
      </DialogClose>
      <Button variant="destructive">Refund $84.00</Button>
    </DialogFooter>
  </DialogContent>
</Dialog>

do: Always give the Dialog a DialogTitle, even if it is visually hidden.
dont: Don't open a Dialog on page load.

components.name: HoverCard
components.summary: A preview card that opens when the pointer rests on, or the keyboard focuses, a link.

props.name: openDelay
props.description: Milliseconds the pointer rests before it opens.

props.name: closeDelay
props.description: Milliseconds before it closes once the pointer leaves.

props.name: side
props.description: Side of the trigger it opens on; it flips when there is no room.

props.name: align
props.description: Alignment against the trigger.

examples.title: Citation preview
examples.code:
The frame order moved to March{" "} [1] Frame supplier decision frame-supplier.md · chunk 1 of 3

We move the frame order to March.
.

do: Make the trigger a link to the same content: the card is a preview, and touch screens never open it.
Keep it short: a title, one line of context and an excerpt.
dont: Don't put buttons or forms in a hover card; it closes when the pointer leaves. Use a Dialog or a Sheet.

components.name: Input
components.summary: A single-line text field. Always paired with a visible label.

props.name: type
props.description: Native input type.

props.name: aria-invalid
props.description: Turns the border and ring to destructive. Pair it with an error message.

examples.title: Search field with label
examples.code:
<label htmlFor="order-search">Search orders</label>
<Input id="order-search" type="search" placeholder="Order number or customer" />

do: Use a visible label; the placeholder is only an example.
dont: Don't use the placeholder as the label.

components.name: Progress
components.summary: A bar that shows how much of a known total is used, such as a budget.

props.name: value
props.description: How much is done, from 0 to max.

props.name: max
props.description: The total the value is measured against.

props.name: variant
props.description: default uses --primary; neutral (--foreground) for budgets and limits; destructive when the total is passed.

examples.title: Budget used
examples.code: $3.30 of $5.00

do: Name the bar with aria-label and write the number next to it: the bar is never the only signal.
dont: Don't use Progress for a wait with no known end; use a spinner with a label.

components.name: ScrollArea
components.summary: A box of fixed height whose content scrolls, with an Atlas scrollbar, such as a side panel of filters.

props.name: type
props.description: When the scrollbar shows: auto whenever the content overflows.

props.name: aria-label
props.description: Name the area when nothing inside takes focus: the viewport becomes a named region keyboard users can scroll.

props.name: orientation
props.description: Add <ScrollBar orientation="horizontal" /> inside for content that scrolls sideways.

examples.title: Neighbors panel
examples.code:
• Frame supplier
  • March production plan
  • Weekly sync, 14 March
  • Dealer pricing sheet
  • Battery warranty terms
  • Color options review
  • Spring launch checklist

do: Give it a fixed height (or max-h) on the root; without one nothing scrolls.
Add aria-label when the content has no links or controls, so the keyboard can reach and scroll it.
dont: Don't wrap the whole page in a ScrollArea; let the page scroll on its own.

components.name: Select
components.summary: Picks one option from a short list.

props.name: position
props.description: popper places the list under the trigger; item-aligned covers it, like a native select.

examples.title: Status filter
examples.code:
<Select defaultValue="all">
  <SelectTrigger aria-label="Status">
    <SelectValue />
  </SelectTrigger>
  <SelectContent>
    <SelectItem value="all">All statuses</SelectItem>
    <SelectItem value="paid">Paid</SelectItem>
  </SelectContent>
</Select>

do: Use Select for 3 to 15 options; fewer fit as buttons or tabs.
dont: Don't use a native <select> next to Atlas controls.

components.name: Sheet
components.summary: A panel that slides in from an edge for details or a form, keeping the page behind.

props.name: side
props.description: Edge the panel slides in from.

examples.title: Order details
examples.code:
<Sheet>
  <SheetTrigger asChild>
    <Button variant="outline">View details</Button>
  </SheetTrigger>
  <SheetContent side="right">
    <SheetHeader>
      <SheetTitle>Order #1042</SheetTitle>
    </SheetHeader>
  </SheetContent>
</Sheet>

do: Use a Sheet for a form or details the user reads next to the list.
dont: Don't stack a Sheet on top of a Dialog.

components.name: Skeleton
components.summary: A grey block that keeps the shape of content while it loads.

examples.title: Loading rows

do: Match the shape and size of the content that will replace it.
Give the region that is loading role="region", a label and aria-busy="true"; the Skeleton itself is hidden from screen readers.
dont: Don't leave a skeleton on screen with no end: after a timeout, show the error state.

components.name: Sonner
components.summary: Toasts: short feedback that confirms an action and disappears on its own.

props.name: position
props.description: Where toasts appear. Mount one Toaster at the root.

props.name: theme
props.description: Sonner's own theme switch. Colors come from the Atlas tokens either way.

examples.title: Confirm a save

do: Confirm what happened in a few words: "Order saved".
dont: Don't put an error the user must act on in a toast; use an Alert.

components.name: Table
components.summary: Rows and columns of data, with a header row.

examples.title: Orders
examples.code: Order Status Total #1042 Paid $84.00

do: Right-align numbers and money.
dont: Don't build tabular data from divs or cards.

components.name: Tabs
components.summary: Switches between views of the same content without leaving the page.

props.name: orientation
props.description: Direction of the tab list and of the arrow keys.

props.name: variant
props.description: default is the segmented track for views inside the product; line is the underline used in docs and code samples.

examples.title: Preview and code
examples.code:
<Tabs defaultValue="preview">
  <TabsList>
    <TabsTrigger value="preview">Preview</TabsTrigger>
    <TabsTrigger value="code">Code</TabsTrigger>
  </TabsList>
  <TabsContent value="preview">…</TabsContent>
  <TabsContent value="code">…</TabsContent>
</Tabs>

do: Keep tab labels to one or two words.
dont: Don't use tabs for steps that must happen in order.

components.name: Textarea
components.summary: A multi-line text field for a comment or a reason. Always with a visible label.

props.name: aria-invalid
props.description: Turns the border and ring to destructive. Pair it with a message under the field.

props.name: rows
props.description: Starting height in lines; the field starts at 88 px and grows with the text.

examples.title: Reason with a label and a hint

do: Give it a visible <label> and link hints and errors with aria-describedby.
dont: Don't use the placeholder as the label.
Don't use a Textarea for a one-line value; use an Input.

components.name: ToggleGroup
components.summary: A row of joined buttons: pick one mode (single), or turn several options on (multiple).

props.name: type
props.description: single is a radio group that always keeps one value once picked; multiple is a toolbar of toggles.

props.name: variant
props.description: outline is the joined segmented control; ghost has no border, for toolbars.

props.name: value
props.description: Controlled value (an array of strings with type="multiple"), with onValueChange.

props.name: value
props.description: The value this item stands for.

examples.title: Search mode
examples.code:
<ToggleGroup type="single" defaultValue="hybrid" aria-label="Search">
  <ToggleGroupItem value="hybrid">Hybrid</ToggleGroupItem>
  <ToggleGroupItem value="vectors">Vectors</ToggleGroupItem>
  <ToggleGroupItem value="graph">Graph</ToggleGroupItem>
</ToggleGroup>

do: Name the group with aria-label or aria-labelledby.
Use it for two to five short options that change the view or the mode in place.
dont: Don't use a ToggleGroup to switch between panels of content; that is Tabs.

components.name: Tooltip
components.summary: A short hint on hover or focus, for icon buttons and abbreviations.

props.name: side
props.description: Side of the trigger the tooltip opens on.

examples.title: Icon button hint
examples.code:
<TooltipProvider>
  <Tooltip>
    <TooltipTrigger asChild>
      <Button variant="ghost" size="icon" aria-label="Copy command">
        <Copy />
      </Button>
    </TooltipTrigger>
    <TooltipContent>Copy command</TooltipContent>
  </Tooltip>
</TooltipProvider>

do: Wrap the app (or the part with tooltips) in one TooltipProvider; a Tooltip outside it throws.
Repeat the aria-label of an icon button in its tooltip.
dont: Don't hide information the user needs inside a tooltip.

rules.title: Color only through tokens
do: Use token classes: bg-background, bg-card, text-foreground, text-muted-foreground, bg-primary, border-border.
Call list_tokens to find the token for a color.
dont: Don't write hex, rgb or named colors (#7c3aed, white).
Don't use Tailwind palette classes such as bg-white or text-slate-900: they ignore the dark theme.

rules.title: One primary button per view
do: Make the main action the default variant and the others outline, secondary or ghost.
dont: Don't put two default buttons side by side.

rules.title: Status is color, icon shape and text together
do: Use the success, warning, info and destructive variants, each with its text and icon.
Map every status of a domain to one variant (paid → success, packing → warning).
dont: Don't show a status by color alone.

rules.title: Labels say what happens
do: Use a verb and an object: "Save order", "Refund $84.00".
dont: Don't use OK, Submit, Yes or No.

rules.title: Import each component from its public file
do: Import from @/components/ui/<file>, the line get_component returns.
dont: Don't import from Atlas internals (src, dist, internal) or straight from Radix.

rules.title: Every field has a visible label
do: Put a label above the field and tie it with htmlFor and id.
dont: Don't rely on the placeholder as the label.

rules.title: Confirm destructive actions
do: Ask in a Dialog that says what will be lost and repeats the action on the button.
dont: Don't delete on a single click without a way back.

rules.title: Tables for tabular data
do: Use Table inside a Card for lists with more than two attributes per item.
dont: Don't build data grids from divs or a grid of cards.

rules.title: A toast confirms, an Alert explains
do: Use toast() after an action succeeds; use an Alert for a state the user must read or fix.
dont: Don't show errors that need action in a toast that disappears.

rules.title: Borders, not shadows
do: Separate surfaces with a 1 px border-border.
dont: Don't add shadows to cards or sections; only overlays (Dialog, Sheet, Popover, toast) have one.

rules.title: Small radius, no pills
do: Keep the component radius: rounded-md on controls and badges, rounded-xl on cards (8.4 px at most).
dont: Don't use rounded-full on buttons, badges or inputs.

rules.title: Amber means example or warning
do: Mark unmeasured numbers with an "Example data" warning badge.
dont: Don't use the warning color for decoration.
